text:
rachel: Heads up  customer reported duplicate tool billing after a stream reconnect. Tool ran once but ledger shows two tool entries.

sylvio: Can you paste the request id and a short timeline?

rachel: req id: r-330c. Timeline: open stream -> toolcall at token 63 -> TCP drop -> reconnect -> resume prefix -> no new tool execution in executor logs but ledger emits second tool charge at reconnect time.

kevin: Do we attach charges by session_id? If resume creates a new session id the router may re-emit an attach event even though the tool is idempotent.

rachel: We do include tool_call.id: "tc-330c". Executor debug: executed once. Router shows two "attach" events.

billing-bot: Alert: anomaly detected in billing stream: duplicate tool charge pattern (ticket BILL-5012).

sylvio: Options: (1) router-side quick cache for recent tool_call ids to avoid re-attaching on resume, (2) ledger post-process dedupe by (customer, tool_call.id, short window), (3) UI suppression of provisional duplicates.

kevin: Router cache seems cleanest for correctness. TTL can be small and in-memory. We'll also add router metrics: attach_emitted vs attach_skipped so we can track frequency.

rachel: Also noticed truncation edge: if server truncates tool output mid-token and then resume emits suffix tokens, our token accounting sometimes counts fragments as separate tokens on ledger. We should standardize to bill only complete tokens emitted to client.

sylvio: Agreed. Action items: (A) rachel to attach traces for r-330c, (B) kevin to prototype router TTL cache PR, (C) billing team to tag suspected duplicates for fast reconciliation (BILL-5012), (D) small console change to hide provisional dupes until confirmed.

rachel: I'll file a short customer note and ping support. Thanks all.
